court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: I Additional Principal Judge, (Incharge of III Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Chennai) - O.S.No.63 of 2014
facts_of_case: The parties were engineering students who got married in a ceremony that the plaintiff claimed was null and void. The defendant used to propose his love towards the plaintiff despite her reluctance. The marriage certificate was declared null and void by the trial court, leading to this appeal.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging undue influence to prove it.
legal_principles.held: When the evidence of D.W.1 to D.W.5 clearly establish the fact that the marriage was validly solemnized and legally registered, the trial Court ought not to have held that the marriage was registered by undue influence, etc.
cited_cases: Mousumi Chakraborty Vs. Subrata Guha Roy, (1991) II DMC 380

legal_principles.principle: The mere registration of a marriage under section 8 of the Hindu Marriage Act does not necessarily prove a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: Whether mere registration of a marriage under section 8 of the Hindu Marriage Act proves the valid marriage?

outcome.result: Appeal filed under Section 19 of Family Court Act read with Section 96 of Code of Civil Procedure against the decree and judgment dated 21.03.2019
outcome.final_order: The final court order was not specified in this excerpt.
